h: How to crack it, and where to go next
p: A few simple habits will give your team the edge. Start by searching thoroughly: drawers, shelves, pockets, under rugs, behind pictures. Pile up anything that looks useful in one place, then start matching things together. Codes usually lead to locks, keys usually lead to boxes, and odd symbols almost always mean something. Keep talking, share everything, and don't be too proud to ask for a hint when you've been stuck for a while.

It's a fun activity for all sorts of occasions. Teenagers often love it as a birthday treat, and it's a refreshing change for families who've done the cinema and bowling a hundred times over. Work teams use it for socials too, and it's a great way to see colleagues in a different light.

Watford is a well-connected town, which makes it easy to meet up. Watford Junction station has fast trains to London Euston and the Midlands, and the Metropolitan line Tube station sits near Cassiobury Park on the other side of town, so groups can arrive by rail or Underground and skip the parking hassle.

There's more to explore once you've escaped. Football fans might want to take a look at Vicarage Road, home of Watford FC, a short walk from the town centre. The Parade, just up from Atria, is a lively stretch of bars and restaurants and home to Watford Colosseum, a historic concert venue. For something more relaxed, the Grand Union Canal winds along the western edge of town and offers peaceful towpath walks. It's a nice contrast to the buzz of the centre after an hour of frantic puzzling.
